newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA TO MEET BRAZIL IN QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA TO MEET BRAZIL IN QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: South American youth champions Argentina set up a clash with favourites Brazil in the world youth soccer championship quarter-finals with a 2-1 win over England on Thursday.
Goals from Riquelme Roman and Aimar Pablo in the first half hour condemned England to the flight home while setting up a mouth-watering clash between South America's two top footballing nations.
"We played very well as a team," Argentine coach Jose Nestor Pakerman said. "I am happy for the boys. This is the best match we have played in this championship.
"It's going to be a tough match for us against Brazil but we have beaten them this year," he added.

Argentina defeated Brazil in the final of the South America youth championship with two goals from Roman, and it was Roman who set up the quarter-final battle against Brazil with a 10th minute penalty.
Pablo added the second 16 minutes later as the South Americans went into the break 2-0 up.
England pulled one back soon after the restart through Liverpool midfielder Jamie Carragher.

"I must say that Argentina played very well," said England coach Ted Powell. "They have many individual players with great skill and talent, and they have shown us the certain areas that we have to improve."
Meanwhile Australia, who defeated Argentina 4-3 in the final game of Group E to win the section, fell to Japan.

A solitary strike by Kashima Antlers forward Atsushi Yanagisawa two minutes before halftime was enough for the World Cup 2002 co-hosts to move into the last eight for the second successive championship.
"It was a very hard game," Japanese coach Masakuni Yamamoto said, "and the weather conditions were very difficult."
The Japanese will travel to southern Johor Baru city where they will play Ghana after the African side ousted the United Arab Emirates 3-0.
A brilliantly taken free-kick by Richard Ackon in the 33rd minute curled over the UAE defensive wall and clipped the under side of the crossbar on its way into the net to give Ghana the lead.

They sealed the match 10 minutes from time when Baba Sule collected a return pass from Peter Ofori-Quaye before thundering the ball past Emirates' keeper Ali Al Yarees. Awudu Issaka completed the scoring in the 88th minute.
Spain scored twice in the last 16 minutes for a 2-0 win against Canada to earn a quarter-final clash with Ireland.
